bulgarian: March always works hard, so I've got to work hard too!

english: Morning [Ari]! I'm helping March with his work! There's nothing these two brothers can't do! *flex*
french: Salut [Ari] ! J'aide March avec son travail ! À deux, rien ne peut nous arrêter ! *contracte ses muscles*
russian: Утро, [Ari]! Помогаю Марту с его делами! Эти два брата всё могут! *показывает мускулы*
bulgarian: Morning [Ari]! I'm helping March with his work! There's nothing these two brothers can't do! *flex*

english: It got so hot... maybe it's time to break out the short shorts.
french: Il fait tellement chaud, là... Il est peut-être temps de sortir le short.
russian: Так жарко стало... может, пора доставать короткие шорты.
bulgarian: It got so hot... maybe it's time to break out the short shorts.

english: Not a drink drink, though. This is hot milk.
french: Mais ce n'est pas le genre de boisson à laquelle tu penses. C'est du lait chaud.
russian: Не пью-пью, это просто горячее молоко.
bulgarian: Not a drink drink, though. This is hot milk.

english: I'm technically working, but Hemlock and Josephine told me to relax, so I'm having a drink.
french: En principe, je devrais être en train de travailler, mais Hemlock et Joséphine m'ont dit de faire une pause, alors je bois un coup.
russian: Формально я на смене, но Хемлок и Джозефина сказали расслабиться, так что я пью.
bulgarian: I'm technically working, but Hemlock and Josephine told me to relax, so I'm having a drink.

english: Everyone asks for a hot toddy in the winter, but no one will tell me! Who's Hot Todd?
french: Tout le monde demande un bon vieux grog, en hiver, mais c'est qui Grog ?
russian: Зимой все постоянно хотят горячего тодди, но никто не говорит мне кто же этот горячий Тодд такой!
bulgarian: Everyone asks for a hot toddy in the winter, but no one will tell me! Who's Hot Todd?

english: Nah, just kidding. Let me know if I can help you out with anything, though.
french: Mais non, je blague. Si je peux t'aider, n'hésite pas.
russian: Шучу. Но если что-то нужно — зови!
bulgarian: Nah, just kidding. Let me know if I can help you out with anything, though.

english: Hey, [Ari]! It's me, Holt! The General Store guy who's always behind the counter! Check out my big mustache!
french: Hé, [Ari] ! C'est moi, Holt ! Le type avec la grosse moustache qui est toujours derrière le comptoir du magasin général !
russian: Эй, [Ari]! Это я, Хольт! Мужик, который постоянно торчит за прилавком универмага. Посмотри, какие у меня усы!
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]! It's me, Holt! The General Store guy who's always behind the counter! Check out my big mustache!

english: So far I'm up to "on the rocks". That means I add ice!
french: Pour le moment, je sais préparer des boissons « frappées ». Ça ne veut pas dire que je leur donne des coups, ça veut dire qu'elles sont bien fraîches !
russian: Пока что я выучил, что, если кто-то просит напиток с камушками, они имеют в виду лёд!
bulgarian: So far I'm up to "on the rocks". That means I add ice!

english: Hemlock and Jo left me in charge of making drinks! I've been practicing.
french: Hemlock et Jo m'ont confié la préparation des boissons ! C'est un bon entraînement.
russian: Хемлок и Джо оставили меня готовить напитки! Я тренируюсь.
bulgarian: Hemlock and Jo left me in charge of making drinks! I've been practicing.

english: I really like this place, [Ari]. It's so cozy and stuff.
french: J'aime beaucoup cet endroit, [Ari]. C'est super confortable, et tout.
russian: Мне тут реально нравится, [Ari]. Так уютно и вообще.
bulgarian: I really like this place, [Ari]. It's so cozy and stuff.

english: March is kind of a lightweight when it comes to drinking, but people seem to like that.
french: March ne supporte pas bien l'alcool, mais j'ai l'impression que ça fait rire les gens.
russian: Март быстро хмелеет, когда дело доходот до выпивки. Но людям это нравится.
bulgarian: March is kind of a lightweight when it comes to drinking, but people seem to like that.

english: And don't worry about ordering too much, I can carry a LOT of food.
french: Et n'hésite pas à commander beaucoup à manger, je peux mettre plein de choses sur mon plateau !
russian: И не бойся заказывать много: я могу нести ОЧЕНЬ много еды.
bulgarian: And don't worry about ordering too much, I can carry a LOT of food.

english: Hey, [Ari]! I'm helping out at the Inn today. Now, what can I get you?
french: Salut, [Ari] ! Je donne un coup de main à l'auberge, aujourd'hui. Alors, qu'est-ce que je te sers ?
russian: Эй, [Ari]! Сегодня помогаю в трактире. Что тебе принести?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]! I'm helping out at the Inn today. Now, what can I get you?

english: Today's special is pretty good, [Ari]. I already had it three times, and it's still pretty special!
french: Le plat du jour est délicieux, [Ari]. J'en ai déjà pris trois fois, et je ne dirais pas non à une quatrième !
russian: Сегодняшнее блюдо дня — супер, [Ari]. Я уже три порции съел, и всё ещё супер!
bulgarian: Today's special is pretty good, [Ari]. I already had it three times, and it's still pretty special!

english: Did I say it right?
french: Quoi ? Je me suis trompé ?
russian: Я правильно сказал?
bulgarian: Did I say it right?

english: Welcome to the Sleepy Dragoon Inn, [Ari]!
french: Bienvenue à l'auberge du Dragon qui mord, [Ari] !
russian: Добро пожаловать в трактир «Сонный драгун», [Ari]!
bulgarian: Welcome to the Sleepy Dragoon Inn, [Ari]!

english: Hey [Ari]! Surprised to see me working here? I'm their favorite part-timer!
french: Salut, [Ari] ! Tu as l'air étonné<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they> de me voir travailler ici. Je suis leur employé à temps partiel préféré !
russian:
Эй, [Ari]!

Удивлены

УдивленаУдивлёнУдивлено, что я тут работаю? Я их любимый подмастерье!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]! Surprised to see me working here? I'm their favorite part-timer!

english: Hemlock says I make a mean bowl of peanuts.
french: Hemlock dit que je verse les cacahuètes dans un bol comme un pro.
russian: Хемлок говорит, я круто подаю арахис.
bulgarian: Hemlock says I make a mean bowl of peanuts.

english: I'm working at the Inn part-time, [Ari]! Let me know if I can get you anything.
french: Je fais un temps partiel à l'auberge, [Ari] ! Dis-moi si tu veux manger quelque chose.
russian: Я подрабатываю в трактире, [Ari]! Скажи, если хочешь что-нибудь.
bulgarian: I'm working at the Inn part-time, [Ari]! Let me know if I can get you anything.

english: Which is kind of a drink too, if you think about it... woah.
french: Qui est aussi une espèce de boisson, quand on y pense... waouh.
russian: Хотя суп — это тоже напиток, если подумать... вау.
bulgarian: Which is kind of a drink too, if you think about it... woah.

english: What can I get you, [Ari]? We got drinks, hot drinks and hot soup!
french: Qu'est-ce que je te sers, [Ari] ? On a des boissons fraîches, des boissons chaudes, et de la soupe !
russian: Что принести, [Ari]? У нас есть напитки, горячие напитки и горячий суп!
bulgarian: What can I get you, [Ari]? We got drinks, hot drinks and hot soup!

english: I can personally recommend the... everything!
french: Personnellement, je recommande... à peu près tout !
russian: Я могу лично порекомендовать... всё!
bulgarian: I can personally recommend the... everything!

english: Take a look at the menu and let me know if you want anything!
french: Jette un œil au menu et dis-moi ce que tu veux !
russian: Глянь меню и скажи, что хочешь!
bulgarian: Take a look at the menu and let me know if you want anything!

english: Oh, hey [Ari]! I'm on shift, so let me know if you want a meal, a drink, or a high five!
french: Bonjour [Ari] ! Je suis de service, alors n'hésite pas si tu veux quelque chose à manger, à boire ou juste qu'on fasse un check !
russian: О, привет, [Ari]! Я на смене, так что говори, если нужен обед, напиток или пятюня!
bulgarian: Oh, hey [Ari]! I'm on shift, so let me know if you want a meal, a drink, or a high five!

english: I'm doing my best, but these push-ups are going to need to come out at some point.
french: Je fais de mon mieux, mais il faudra que je fasse quelques pompes à un moment donné.
russian: Я стараюсь, но рано или поздно точно захочу начать отжиматься.
bulgarian: I'm doing my best, but these push-ups are going to need to come out at some point.

english: Hemlock said I have to behave professionally when I'm working an inn shift.
french: Hemlock m'a dit que je devais rester pro jusqu'à la fin de mon service, à l'auberge.
russian: Хемлок сказал, что на смене надо вести себя профессионально.
bulgarian: Hemlock said I have to behave professionally when I'm working an inn shift.

english: Like... so much food!
french: Des... montagnes de nourriture !
russian: Даже... очень много еды!
bulgarian: Like... so much food!

english: You hungry? We got food.
french: Tu as faim ? On a de quoi manger.
russian:
Голодный

ГолоднаяГолодныйГолодное? У нас есть еда.
bulgarian: You hungry? We got food.

english: Oh, it's you [Ari]! You live here!
french: Oh, c'est toi, [Ari] ! Tu vis ici, on dirait.
russian: Ой, это ты, [Ari]! Ты же тут живёшь!
bulgarian: Oh, it's you [Ari]! You live here!

english: The Sleeping Dragon Inn welcomes you to Mistria, esteemed guest!
french: L'auberge du Dragon qui dort vous souhaite la bienvenue, <she>chère cliente</she><he>cher client</he><they>cher·ère client·e</they> !
russian: Трактир «Спящий дракон» рад приветствовать вас в Мистрии, почтенный гость!
bulgarian: The Sleeping Dragon Inn welcomes you to Mistria, esteemed guest!

english: [Ari]! You're here, nice. Let me know if I can get you anything, okay?
french: [Ari] ! C'est sympa de te voir ici. Si tu veux commander quelque chose, n'hésite pas, d'accord ?
russian:
[Ari]! Хорошо, что ты

зашли

зашлазашёлзашло. Скажи, если тебе что-нибудь нужно, ладно?
bulgarian: [Ari]! You're here, nice. Let me know if I can get you anything, okay?

english: It's nice to do all these different jobs around town... it really helps me understand what everyone is all about.
french: J'aime bien faire tout un tas de petits boulots différents en ville... Ça m'aide à comprendre la façon de fonctionner de chacun.
russian: Мне нравится подрабатывать там и сям по городу... Сразу лучше понимаешь, что у кого на уме.
bulgarian: It's nice to do all these different jobs around town... it really helps me understand what everyone is all about.

english: I think I need to change up my routine... I've been skipping leg day too much. From now on, it's ALL legs!
french: Je crois que je reverrai ma routine... Ça fait longtemps que je n'ai pas travaillé les cuisses. Dorénavant, je mise TOUT sur les cuisses !
russian: Надо менять программу... я слишком часто пропускал день ног. С этого дня — только ноги!
bulgarian: I think I need to change up my routine... I've been skipping leg day too much. From now on, it's ALL legs!

english: That's when I'd find the coolest rocks!
french: C'est là-bas que je trouvais les plus belles pierres !
russian: Там я находил самые крутые камни!
bulgarian: That's when I'd find the coolest rocks!

english: I used to get lost down in the Mines a lot, but I didn't mind.
french: Je me perdais très souvent dans les mines, avant, mais ça ne me gênait pas plus que ça.
russian: Я раньше часто терялся в шахтах, но мне это нравилось.
bulgarian: I used to get lost down in the Mines a lot, but I didn't mind.

english: These days, I can really enjoy the walk!
french: Maintenant, j'aime venir m'y balader !
russian: А сейчас, наконец, могу гулять тут без дела.
bulgarian: These days, I can really enjoy the walk!

english: I used to come through here all the time, when I worked down in the Mines.
french: Je venais tout le temps ici quand je travaillais à la mine.
russian: Я часто здесь ходил, когда работал в шахтах.
bulgarian: I used to come through here all the time, when I worked down in the Mines.

english: You've probably seen stuff down there that we never did! That's pretty cool.
french: Tu as dû voir des choses qu'on n'a jamais vues, nous ! C'est vraiment cool.
russian:
Ты, наверное,

встречали

встречалавстречалвстречало там такие штуки, которых мы никогда не видали! Круто.
bulgarian: You've probably seen stuff down there that we never did! That's pretty cool.

english: Even when the Mines were open, Errol and I didn't go too deep.
french: Même quand la mine était encore en activité, Errol et moi ne descendions jamais trop bas.
russian: Даже до закрытия шахт мы с Эрролом не очень глубоко заходили.
bulgarian: Even when the Mines were open, Errol and I didn't go too deep.

english: Wow [Ari], you do a lot of walking! That's super cool!
french: Waouh, [Ari], je te vois beaucoup marcher ! C'est vraiment cool !
russian: Вау, [Ari], ты так много ходишь! Это круто!
bulgarian: Wow [Ari], you do a lot of walking! That's super cool!

english: I love trees, [Ari]... they put me all at peace and stuff. Kind of like when I look at cool rocks.
french: [Ari], j'adore les arbres... Ça m'apaise. Un peu comme quand je regarde des super pierres.
russian: Я люблю деревья, [Ari]... они успокаивают, как крутые камни.
bulgarian: I love trees, [Ari]... they put me all at peace and stuff. Kind of like when I look at cool rocks.

english: March got called out on a job today, so I'm holding it down until he gets back. Let me know if you need anything, [Ari]!
french: March s'est absenté pour un boulot, donc je suis sur le pont jusqu'à son retour. Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, n'hésite pas, [Ari].
russian: Март сегодня ушёл на заказ, так что я тут за старшего. Скажи, если что нужно, [Ari]!
bulgarian: March got called out on a job today, so I'm holding it down until he gets back. Let me know if you need anything, [Ari]!

english: I wonder if I could run laps in here...
french: Je me demande si je pourrais y faire mon footing...
russian: Интересно, можно ли тут побегать кругами...
bulgarian: I wonder if I could run laps in here...

english: Lady Adeline always says the Manor grounds are open to everyone, so I thought I'd check it out!
french: Dame Adeline dit que les jardins du manoir sont ouverts à tous, alors je me suis dit que j'allais y faire un petit tour !
russian: Леди Аделина всегда говорит, что территория особняка открыта для всех, так что я решил заглянуть!
bulgarian: Lady Adeline always says the Manor grounds are open to everyone, so I thought I'd check it out!

english: Red's his color!
french: C'est sa couleur préférée !
russian: Красный — его цвет!
bulgarian: Red's his color!

english: March gets all fired up when the leaves turn red.
french: Quand les feuilles virent au rouge, March est surexcité !
russian: Март всегда загорается, когда листья становятся красными.
bulgarian: March gets all fired up when the leaves turn red.

english: Look at my bro go! No one swings a hammer like him!
french: Regarde cette économie de gestes ! Personne ne bat le fer comme mon frère !
russian: Смотри, как мой бро работает! Никто так молотом не машет!
bulgarian: Look at my bro go! No one swings a hammer like him!

english: He doesn't come out and say it so directly...
french: Il ne le dira pas ouvertement...
russian: Он не признаётся в этом прямо...
bulgarian: He doesn't come out and say it so directly...

english: But it's obviously because of you!
french: Mais c'est évident que c'est grâce à toi !
russian: Но это точно благодаря тебе!
bulgarian: But it's obviously because of you!

english: March seems really happy, lately.
french: March a l'air heureux ces derniers temps.
russian: Март в последнее время выглядит веселее.
bulgarian: March seems really happy, lately.

english: He acted like he wasn't sure what you'd like... but he ended up deciding to go with his own idea to make a helmet.
french: Il disait ne pas trop savoir ce qui te plairait... mais finalement, il est resté sur son idée de fabriquer un casque.
russian: Он говорил, будто сомневается, что тебе понравится... Но в итоге выбрал свою собственную идею сделать шлем.
bulgarian: He acted like he wasn't sure what you'd like... but he ended up deciding to go with his own idea to make a helmet.

english: I don't get it, why wouldn't he know the preferences of the person he's always talking about?
french: Je ne comprends pas. Comment il ne connaîtrait pas les goûts de la personne dont il parle tout le temps ?
russian: Не понимаю его. Как можно не знать, что понравится человеку, о котором ты всё время болтаешь?
bulgarian: I don't get it, why wouldn't he know the preferences of the person he's always talking about?

english: The other day, March was asking everyone what they thought you'd want as a present.
french: L'autre jour, March a demandé à tout le monde quel cadeau il pouvait t'offrir.
russian: Март на днях спрашивал у всех, какой тебе лучше подарить подарок.
bulgarian: The other day, March was asking everyone what they thought you'd want as a present.

english: My bro works really hard... I sure wish he would rest just as hard!
french: Mon frère travaille vraiment très dur... J'aimerais bien qu'il se repose avec autant d'insistance !
russian: Мой бро много работает... вот бы он отдыхал так же много!
bulgarian: My bro works really hard... I sure wish he would rest just as hard!

english: I try to give March space at the forge when I can. He really likes getting into the zone, you know?
french: J'essaie de laisser March tranquille à la forge autant que possible. Il a vraiment besoin de se concentrer pour être à fond.
russian: Я стараюсь давать Марту пространство в кузнице. Он любит «входить в поток», знаешь?
bulgarian: I try to give March space at the forge when I can. He really likes getting into the zone, you know?

english: That and we're related, I guess.
french: Et peut-être aussi parce qu'on est de la même famille.
russian: Ну, и потому, что мы родственники, наверное.
bulgarian: That and we're related, I guess.

english: The real reason March keeps me around is because I have all the melting points of ores memorized.
french: La vraie raison pour laquelle March m'héberge, c'est parce que je connais par cœur le point de fusion de tous les métaux.
russian: На самом деле Март держит меня рядом потому, что я знаю все температуры плавления руды.
bulgarian: The real reason March keeps me around is because I have all the melting points of ores memorized.

english: Morning, [Ari]! Working hard? Yeah you are!
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! Ça bosse dur ? Je vois que oui !
russian: Утро, [Ari]! Трудимся? Вот это да!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Working hard? Yeah you are!

english: A morning bath is great for getting that winter chill out!
french: Un petit bain matinal permet de se débarrasser de la fraîcheur hivernale !
russian: Утренняя ванна — лучшее средство от зимнего холода!
bulgarian: A morning bath is great for getting that winter chill out!

english: Nothing like a morning run to wake the body up!  Your body looks super awake too, [Ari]! Nice!
french: Rien de tel qu'un footing à la fraîche pour remettre la machine en route ! Toi, tu as l'air en pleine forme, [Ari] ! Super !
russian: Нет ничего лучше утренней пробежки, чтобы разбудить тело! Твоё тело тоже супербодрое, [Ari]! Класс!
bulgarian: Nothing like a morning run to wake the body up!  Your body looks super awake too, [Ari]! Nice!

english: It's super bright! Like fluorite!
french: Il a une lueur particulière. Comme la fluorine !
russian: Оно такое яркое! Прямо как флюорит!
bulgarian: It's super bright! Like fluorite!

english: I love that morning sunshine!
french: J'adore le soleil du matin !
russian: Обожаю утреннее солнце!
bulgarian: I love that morning sunshine!

english: Awww yeah, [Ari]... my muscles feel SUPER good... wanna see?
french: Ah ouais, c'est bon ça, [Ari]... Je ressens une sensation hyper agréable dans mes muscles... Ça se remarque ?
russian: Ооо да, [Ari]... мои мышцы просто КАЙФ... хочешь посмотреть?
bulgarian: Awww yeah, [Ari]... my muscles feel SUPER good... wanna see?

english: Now I look at it and I'm like... wow... it's full of even cooler rocks!
french: En le regardant maintenant, je me dis... waouh... il est plein de pierres encore plus cool.
russian: А сейчас я смотрю на него и думаю: «Ого... тут теперь камни гораздо круче!»
bulgarian: Now I look at it and I'm like... wow... it's full of even cooler rocks!

english: Back when this building was the Mines' storehouse, it was mostly full of rocks.
french: À l'époque où ce bâtiment était l'entrepôt de la mine, on y trouvait presque que des pierres.
russian: Раньше, когда в этом здании был шахтёрский склад, тут в основном хранились камни.
bulgarian: Back when this building was the Mines' storehouse, it was mostly full of rocks.

english: There's lots of heavy stuff in there!
french: Il y a des tas de trucs lourds, là-dedans !
russian: Там куча тяжёлых штук!
bulgarian: There's lots of heavy stuff in there!

english: Oh, hey [Ari]. I came by to help Errol rearrange some of the Museum's archive.
french: Oh, salut [Ari]. Je suis passé aider Errol à réorganiser des archives du musée.
russian: О, привет, [Ari]. Я тут заскочил помочь Эрролу с перестановками в музейном архиве.
bulgarian: Oh, hey [Ari]. I came by to help Errol rearrange some of the Museum's archive.

english: Or are you donating something?
french: Ou bien tu es là pour donner quelque chose ?
russian: Или ты что-то сдаёшь?
bulgarian: Or are you donating something?

english: I'm helping out today, so let me know if you need anything!
french: Je donne un coup de main au musée aujourd'hui, alors si tu veux quelque chose, fais-moi signe !
russian: Сегодня я помогаю, так что говори, если что-то нужно!
bulgarian: I'm helping out today, so let me know if you need anything!

english: Oh whoa, you donated some of these! Maybe you can explain them to me!

russian: Найти такой идеальный камень — настоящая редкость! Только посмотри на цвет! На прозрачность! Ни одной трещинки! Я мог бы смотреть на него весь день!
bulgarian: It's pretty rare to find a gem as perfect as this! Look at the color! And the clarity! Not a single fracture. I could look at this all day!

english: Thanks, [Ari]! I'll treat this so good!
french: Merci, [Ari] ! J'en prendrai bien soin !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]! Я буду беречь его как следует!
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari]! I'll treat this so good!

english: Look at the perfect formation of this ore! It's like a piece of art, made by nature! And it's for me?
french: Ce minerai n'a pas un défaut ! C'est comme une œuvre d'art créée par la nature ! C'est vraiment pour moi ?
russian: Посмотри на идеальную форму этой руды! Прямо произведение искусства от природы! И это — мне?
bulgarian: Look at the perfect formation of this ore! It's like a piece of art, made by nature! And it's for me?

english: This is going straight into my collection!
french: Ça va tout droit dans ma collection.
russian: Это сразу пойдёт в мою коллекцию!
bulgarian: This is going straight into my collection!

english: So cool, [Ari]! I never came across anything this perfect when I worked in the Mines. You must have gone real deep to find it!
french: Merci, [Ari] ! Je n'avais encore jamais vu quelque chose d'aussi beau, même quand j'étais mineur. Tu as dû descendre très profond pour récupérer ça !
russian: Так круто, [Ari]! Даже в шахтах я не находил ничего такого совершенного. Тебе, наверное, глубоко копать пришлось.
bulgarian: So cool, [Ari]! I never came across anything this perfect when I worked in the Mines. You must have gone real deep to find it!

english: Hey, thanks!
french: Génial, merci !
russian: Эй, спасибо!
bulgarian: Hey, thanks!

english: Wow, thanks! Let's see, this one's... sandstone! You can tell by how grainy it looks and how gritty it feels.
french: Waouh, merci ! Vu l'aspect granuleux et la texture abrasive, je dirais que c'est... du grès !
russian: Вау, спасибо! Так, это у нас... песчаник! Узнаётся по зернистости и шероховатой текстуре.
bulgarian: Wow, thanks! Let's see, this one's... sandstone! You can tell by how grainy it looks and how gritty it feels.

english: Ooh, a rock! Looks like limestone to me. See how easy it is to scratch?
french: Oh, une pierre ! C'est sûrement du calcaire. Tu vois comme elle se casse facilement ?
russian: О, камень! Похоже на известняк. Видишь, как легко царапается?
bulgarian: Ooh, a rock! Looks like limestone to me. See how easy it is to scratch?

english: Thanks, [Ari]! This one's gneiss. Nice!
french: Merci, [Ari] ! Ça, c'est du gneiss. Très intéressant !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]! Это гнейс. Класс!
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari]! This one's gneiss. Nice!

english: Quartzite? For me? Thanks, I'll add it to my collection of hard, nonfoliated metamorphic rocks!
french: C'est pour moi ce quartzite ? Merci, il rejoindra ma collection de roches dures métamorphiques non foliées !
russian: Кварцит? Для меня? Спасибо, добавлю в коллекцию твёрдых метаморфических пород!
bulgarian: Quartzite? For me? Thanks, I'll add it to my collection of hard, nonfoliated metamorphic rocks!

english: Ooh, what's this? Granite? Sweet. You can tell by the shiny bits, those are crystal! Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Oooh, c'est du granit ? Génial. On le reconnaît aux petits points brillants, c'est des cristaux. Merci, [Ari] !
russian: О-о, что это? Гранит? Круто. Блестящие вкрапления — это кристаллы! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Ooh, what's this? Granite? Sweet. You can tell by the shiny bits, those are crystal! Thanks, [Ari]!

english: This stone is pretty dark... fine grain... low in silica... it's basalt! Thanks [Ari], you're really helping me grow my rock collection.
french: Un couleur sombre, un grain fin, une teneur en silice faible... C'est du basalte ! Merci, [Ari]. Tu m'aides vraiment beaucoup pour ma collection de minéraux.
russian: Камень тёмный... мелкозернистый... мало кремния... это базальт! Спасибо, [Ari], ты отлично пополняешь мою коллекцию!
bulgarian: This stone is pretty dark... fine grain... low in silica... it's basalt! Thanks [Ari], you're really helping me grow my rock collection.

english: Let's see... smooth to the touch... alternating bands of light and dark... pretty hard... this is schist! Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Voyons voir... La surface est lisse... Il y a une succession de lignes claires et sombres... Elle est assez dure... C'est du schiste ! Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Так... гладкий на ощупь... чередуются светлые и тёмные полосы... довольно твёрдый... это сланец! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Let's see... smooth to the touch... alternating bands of light and dark... pretty hard... this is schist! Thanks, [Ari]!

english: Glassy luster, a bit rectangular... got to be feldspar. Cool! Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Une surface brillante, une forme légèrement rectangulaire... C'est du feldspath, aucun doute là-dessus. Super ! Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Стеклянный блеск, прямоугольная форма... должно быть, полевой шпат. Круто! Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Glassy luster, a bit rectangular... got to be feldspar. Cool! Thanks, [Ari]!

english: [Ari]. My friend. Why would you give me a $Rockbiter$? Do you secretly hate rocks or something?
french: [Ari], on est amis, non ? Pourquoi tu m'offres un $croqueroche$ ? Au fond, tu détestes les pierres, c'est ça ?
russian:
[Ari].

Дружище

подарили

подарилаподарилподарило мне $камнегрыза$? Ты что, на самом деле втайне ненавидишь камни?
bulgarian: [Ari]. My friend. Why would you give me a $Rockbiter$? Do you secretly hate rocks or something?

english: I like to put a little bit of butter in Darcy's coffee. Gives me energy!
french: Quand je prends un café chez Darcy, j'aime bien y ajouter un peu de beurre. Ça me donne la pêche !
russian: Я люблю добавлять немного масла в кофе Дарси. Придаёт энергии!
bulgarian: I like to put a little bit of butter in Darcy's coffee. Gives me energy!

english: Darcy's always trying to get me to try something called tea, but leaves? In water? Is it a kind of soup?
french: Darcy essaie toujours de me faire goûter son « thé ». Apparemment, c'est des feuilles dans de l'eau. Comme une espèce de soupe ?
russian: Дарси всегда уговаривает меня попробовать что-то под названием «чай», но... листья? В воде? Это что, что-то вроде супа?
bulgarian: Darcy's always trying to get me to try something called tea, but leaves? In water? Is it a kind of soup?

english: Before the earthquake, Errol and I used to make a big pot of coffee before a long day in the Mines... don't tell Errol I said so, but Darcy's is sooo much better.
french: Avant le tremblement de terre, Errol et moi, on se buvait une grosse cafetière avant de descendre à la mine... Ne dis rien à Errol, mais le café de Darcy est bien meilleur.
russian: До землетрясения мы с Эрролом всегда варили огромный чан кофе перед сменой в шахте... не говори Эрролу, но кофе у Дарси ГОРА-А-АЗДО вкуснее.
bulgarian: Before the earthquake, Errol and I used to make a big pot of coffee before a long day in the Mines... don't tell Errol I said so, but Darcy's is sooo much better.

english: March says I should stop drinking coffee because it makes me anxious... I start asking myself stuff like "ARE my muscles cool enough?" They totally are, though.
french: March me dit d'arrêter le café parce que ça me rend anxieux. Je ressasse toujours des questions du genre « mes muscles sont-ils assez gros ? », alors que la réponse est évidente.
russian: Март говорит, что мне надо бросить кофе, потому что я начинаю волноваться... типа: «А точно ли мои мышцы крутые?!» А они точно крутые.
bulgarian: March says I should stop drinking coffee because it makes me anxious... I start asking myself stuff like "ARE my muscles cool enough?" They totally are, though.

english: Honestly, I don't get fashion much... Louis is always pumped to pick for me, though.
french: À vrai dire, la mode et moi, ça fait deux... mais Louis s'empresse toujours de choisir mes tenues pour moi.
russian: Честно, я не особо понимаю моду... но Луи всегда в восторге, когда подбирает мне одежду.
bulgarian: Honestly, I don't get fashion much... Louis is always pumped to pick for me, though.

english: Louis is always measuring my biceps and letting out my sleeves... I guess he learned his lesson after the first time I burst out of a jacket.
french: Louis prend toujours les mensurations de mes biceps pour élargir les manches... Je crois qu'il a compris la leçon quand j'ai déchiré une veste.
russian: Луи вечно меряет мои бицепсы и распарывает рукава... видимо, выучил урок, после того, как я в первый раз разорвал пиджак.
bulgarian: Louis is always measuring my biceps and letting out my sleeves... I guess he learned his lesson after the first time I burst out of a jacket.

english: I wonder if Louis can patch my boots? They're getting worn out...
french: Je me demande si Louis pourrait rafistoler mes bottes. Elles commencent à être usées...
russian: Интересно, Луи сможет подлатать мои ботинки? Они изрядно поизносились...
bulgarian: I wonder if Louis can patch my boots? They're getting worn out...

english: I didn't even get it from him... he just doesn't like it when people do that.
french: Pourtant, elle ne venait même pas de chez lui... Il n'aime pas quand les gens font ça.
russian: Я её даже не у него брал... но он просто ненавидит, когда так делают.
bulgarian: I didn't even get it from him... he just doesn't like it when people do that.

english: Louis was NOT happy when I tore the sleeves off one of my shirts...
french: Louis s'est vraiment mis en pétard quand j'ai déchiré les manches d'une de mes chemises.
russian: Луи был очень недоволен, когда я оторвал рукава у рубашки...
bulgarian: Louis was NOT happy when I tore the sleeves off one of my shirts...

english: Hey [Ari]! I just got done hauling furniture around Merri's booth... let me know if you need help carrying something home! Happy to help.
french: Salut [Ari] ! Je viens juste de finir de réagencer le stand de Merri. Fais-moi signe quand tu as quelque chose de lourd à transporter chez toi ! Si je peux aider...
russian: Эй, [Ari]! Я только что перетаскивал мебель у лавки Мэрри... если надо что-то донести — обращайся! С радостью помогу!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]! I just got done hauling furniture around Merri's booth... let me know if you need help carrying something home! Happy to help.

english: Hayden and I take turns helping Merri out with getting all her furniture to her booth.
french: Hayden et moi, on se relaie pour aider Merri à transporter les meubles jusqu'à son stand.
russian: Мы с Хейденом по очереди помогаем Мэрри тащить мебель к её лавке.
bulgarian: Hayden and I take turns helping Merri out with getting all her furniture to her booth.

english: Maybe I should get another shelf from Merri... I've got more crystals I want to display...
french: Je devrais peut-être acheter une nouvelle étagère à Merri... J'ai encore des cristaux à exposer...
russian: Может, стоит взять у Мэрри ещё одну полку... у меня накопилось кристаллов для витрины...
bulgarian: Maybe I should get another shelf from Merri... I've got more crystals I want to display...

english: Merri thinks I don't know how strong she is... she could move all this furniture herself! But I like carrying heavy stuff, and it's fun to help her out.
french: Merri s'imagine que je ne connais pas sa force... Elle pourrait déplacer tous ces meubles elle-même ! C'est juste que j'aime bien porter des trucs lourds.
russian: Мэрри думает, я не замечаю, насколько она сильная... она могла бы всё это сама перетаскать! Но мне нравится носить тяжести, и помогать ей — весело.
bulgarian: Merri thinks I don't know how strong she is... she could move all this furniture herself! But I like carrying heavy stuff, and it's fun to help her out.

english: I wonder if she'd want to work out with me and Hayden...
french: Je me demande si ça l'intéresserait de faire de la muscu avec Hayden et moi...
russian: Интересно, согласится ли она потренироваться со мной и Хейденом...
bulgarian: I wonder if she'd want to work out with me and Hayden...

english: If Stillwell ever tells you he feels "the darkness receding" when you're around, don't worry about it. That's how he describes friendship!
bulgarian: If Stillwell ever tells you he feels "the darkness receding" when you're around, don't worry about it. That's how he describes friendship!

english: Stillwell told me that I would learn to cherish something new today, and you know what? I found a brand new muscle! Want to see?
bulgarian: Stillwell told me that I would learn to cherish something new today, and you know what? I found a brand new muscle! Want to see?

english: Stillwell told me "not everything that glitters is gold, beware the allure of fool's gold"... Joke's on him, I love pyrite!
bulgarian: Stillwell told me "not everything that glitters is gold, beware the allure of fool's gold"... Joke's on him, I love pyrite!

english: I tried jogging with Stillwell once, but his robes were so heavy he passed out... Afterwards he told me he'd "portended a great conflagration", whatever that means.
bulgarian: I tried jogging with Stillwell once, but his robes were so heavy he passed out... Afterwards he told me he'd "portended a great conflagration", whatever that means.

english: The kind you eat, obviously!
french: Bah, le type qui se mange !
russian: Очевидно — съедобную!
bulgarian: The kind you eat, obviously!

english: I told Taliferro I like food, and he asked what kind...
french: J'ai dit à Taliferro que j'aimais la nourriture. Il m'a demandé quel type...
russian: Я сказал Талиферро, что люблю еду, а он спросил: «Какую?»
bulgarian: I told Taliferro I like food, and he asked what kind...

english: So maybe Taliferro just needs a big bro!
french: Taliferro a peut-être juste besoin d'un grand frère !
russian: Может, ему просто нужен старший бро!
bulgarian: So maybe Taliferro just needs a big bro!

english: I don't really like how Taliferro talks to people, but then I thought he sounds kinda like March on a bad day.
french: Je n'aime pas la façon dont Taliferro parle aux gens, puis j'ai trouvé que March était pareil dans ses mauvais jours.
russian: Мне ужасно не нравится, как Талиферро обращается с людьми, он звучит, как Март в плохой день.
bulgarian: I don't really like how Taliferro talks to people, but then I thought he sounds kinda like March on a bad day.

english: But it tastes awesome! How does he do that, [Ari]?
french: Mais c'est super bon ! Comment fait-il, [Ari] ?
russian: Но вкус потрясный! Как у него это получается, [Ari]?
bulgarian: But it tastes awesome! How does he do that, [Ari]?

english: Taliferro's cooking makes me kinda sad... it's always all small and doesn't look like food.
french: La cuisine de Taliferro ne me met pas en appétit... Il n'y a rien à manger et ça ne ressemble pas à de la nourriture.
russian: Блюда у Талиферро всегда выглядят так грустно... Они такие маленькие и не похожи на еду.
bulgarian: Taliferro's cooking makes me kinda sad... it's always all small and doesn't look like food.

english: But [Ari], I help at the forge! I can totally stand the heat!
french: Mais je travaille avec March, [Ari] ! S'il y a bien une chose que je supporte, c'est la pression !
russian: Но, [Ari], я же помогаю в кузнице! Я прекрасно выношу жар!
bulgarian: But [Ari], I help at the forge! I can totally stand the heat!

english: Taliferro told me that if I can't stand the heat, to get out of the kitchen...
french: Taliferro m'a dit que si je ne supportais pas la pression, je n'avais qu'à sortir de la cuisine...
russian: Талиферро мне сказал: не выносишь жар — не суйся на кухню...
bulgarian: Taliferro told me that if I can't stand the heat, to get out of the kitchen...

english: Vera says she can dye my hair blonde, but what if I dyed it the same color as March?
french: Vera m'a proposé de me teindre en blond, mais si je me faisais plutôt la même couleur que March ?
russian: Вера говорит, может покрасить мои волосы в светлый цвет. Но что, если я покрашусь в тот же цвет, что у Марта?
bulgarian: Vera says she can dye my hair blonde, but what if I dyed it the same color as March?

english: March goes to see Vera whenever she's at the Saturday Market... he likes to put the red back in before his roots start to show.
french: March va toujours voir Vera quand elle est au marché, le samedi. Il se fait teindre les cheveux avant qu'on voie les racines.
russian: Март ходит к Вере каждый раз, когда она на Субботнем базаре... он любит подкрашивать свои красные волосы, когда корни отрастают.
bulgarian: March goes to see Vera whenever she's at the Saturday Market... he likes to put the red back in before his roots start to show.

english: I'll leave the hair-dyeing to my bro... I like to go au naturel!
french: Les colorations, je laisse ça à mon frère... Moi, je préfère ma couleur naturelle.
russian: Оставлю покраску моему бро... сам я люблю естественность!
bulgarian: I'll leave the hair-dyeing to my bro... I like to go au naturel!

english: Don't sweat it, Vera has plenty of hair dye... I helped haul the barrels in myself.
french: Vera a énormément de couleurs différentes... Je le sais, parce que je l'ai aidée à transporter les tonneaux.
russian: Не переживай, у Веры полно краски... я сам помогал таскать бочки!
bulgarian: Don't sweat it, Vera has plenty of hair dye... I helped haul the barrels in myself.

english: I mean, a super special stone? You know I've gotta have it!
french: Tu imagines, une pierre d'exception ? Il me la faut !
russian: Супернеобычный камень — это мне точно надо!
bulgarian: I mean, a super special stone? You know I've gotta have it!

english: Wheedle offered to sell me a super special =Stone= for 1000t! He said it was a real bargain!
french: Wheedle m'a proposé une =pierre= d'exception pour 1 000 tesserae. Il a dit que c'était l'affaire du siècle !
russian: Хлюст предложил мне купить супернеобычный =камень= за 1000 тессер! Сказал, что это ещё дёшево!
bulgarian: Wheedle offered to sell me a super special =Stone= for 1000t! He said it was a real bargain!

english: I don't know, [Ari]... what's the conversion rate for Wheedle Bucks? Is it good?
french: Je ne sais pas, [Ari]... Ça donne quoi, le cours du Wheedollar ? Plutôt bon ?
russian: Не знаю, [Ari]... Какой сейчас у хлюстолларов курс? Хороший?
bulgarian: I don't know, [Ari]... what's the conversion rate for Wheedle Bucks? Is it good?

english: Wheedle wanted to hire me, and said he'd pay me in Wheedle Bucks!
french: Wheedle voudrait m'engager. Il a dit qu'il me paierait en Wheedollars !
russian: Хлюст хотел меня нанять и сказал, что будет платить хлюстолларами!
bulgarian: Wheedle wanted to hire me, and said he'd pay me in Wheedle Bucks!

english: So of course I bought it!
french: Donc, je lui ai acheté !
russian: Разумеется, я его купил!
bulgarian: So of course I bought it!

english: Wheedle was selling something he swore was a rainbow dragon scale... but I took a closer look and it was a regular piece of bismuth.
french: Wheedle vendait ce qu'il assurait être une écaille de dragon arc-en-ciel. À y regarder de plus près, c'était un simple morceau de bismuth.
russian: Хлюст продавал штучку, которую называл чешуёй радужного дракона... Но я присмотрелся поближе и увидел, что это обыкновенный висмут.
bulgarian: Wheedle was selling something he swore was a rainbow dragon scale... but I took a closer look and it was a regular piece of bismuth.

english: Of course I bought it! I'll let you know how it goes, [Ari]!
french: Bien entendu, j'en ai acheté. Je te dirai ce que ça donne, [Ari].
russian: И я, конечно же, купил! Я тебе расскажу, если сработает, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Of course I bought it! I'll let you know how it goes, [Ari]!

english: Wheedle said I should buy some $Fast Food$, so I run faster when I go for a morning jog...
french: Wheedle m'a conseillé les $encas sur le pouce$ pour courir plus vite pendant mon jogging matinal...
russian: Хлюст сказал, что, если я куплю $фастфуд$, то буду бегать быстрее во время пробежки по утрам...
bulgarian: Wheedle said I should buy some $Fast Food$, so I run faster when I go for a morning jog...

english: She was all like, "booooowraaaaar" with it!
french: Elle arrivait à faire des « bouuuuuouiiiiin », avec !
russian: Недавно она сделала такое: «пау-ви-и-и-иу»!
bulgarian: She was all like, "booooowraaaaar" with it!

english: Zorel can really wail on that lute of hers!
french: Zorel sait vraiment tirer des sons plaintifs de son luth !
russian: Зорель извлекает из своей лютни такие стоны!
bulgarian: Zorel can really wail on that lute of hers!

english: You've got a good eye for cool rocks.
french: Tu as l'œil pour les belles pierres.
russian: У тебя отличный вкус на крутые камни.
bulgarian: You've got a good eye for cool rocks.

english: I was at the Museum earlier and I saw that $Faceted Rock Gem$! Did you donate that, [Ari]?
french: Je suis passé au musée, il n'y a pas longtemps, et j'ai vu la $pierre de roche ciselée$ ! C'est toi qui l'as trouvée, [Ari] ?
russian:
Я был в музее и видел этот $гранёный камень$! Это ты

пожертвовали

пожертвовалапожертвовалпожертвовало, [Ari]?
bulgarian: I was at the Museum earlier and I saw that $Faceted Rock Gem$! Did you donate that, [Ari]?

english: That $Iron Fish$ at the Museum... how come it doesn't sink in the water?
french: Ce $poisson de fer$, au musée... Comment ça se fait qu'il ne coule pas dans l'eau ?
russian:
Видели

ВиделаВиделВидело $рыбу-железку$ в музее? Почему она не тонет в воде?..
bulgarian: That $Iron Fish$ at the Museum... how come it doesn't sink in the water?

english: I've heard of ringing rocks... rock guys call them lithophonic rocks...
french: J'ai déjà entendu parler de pierres qui chantent, les spécialistes appellent ça des phonolithes...
russian: Я слышал про поющие камни... Кто разбирается, ещё называют их «звенящие камни»...
bulgarian: I've heard of ringing rocks... rock guys call them lithophonic rocks...

english: But a windy crystal? That's new to me!
french: Mais un cristal empli de vent ? C'est une nouveauté !
russian: Но кристалл со звуком ветра? Это что-то новенькое!
bulgarian: But a windy crystal? That's new to me!

english: That $Mist Crystal$ at the Museum makes a sound like gusting wind when you hold it to your ear.
french: Ce $cristal de brume$, au musée, on entend comme des bourrasques de vent quand on le colle à l'oreille.
russian: В музее есть $туманный кристалл$. Он издаёт звук, как ревущий ветер, если его приложить к уху.
bulgarian: That $Mist Crystal$ at the Museum makes a sound like gusting wind when you hold it to your ear.

english: My natural enemy... whoa...
french: Eh bien, c'est mon ennemi...
russian: Мой природный враг... вау...
bulgarian: My natural enemy... whoa...

english: Errol said that new fish over at the Museum is called a $Rockbiter$... on account of it chews up rocks?
french: Errol m'a dit que le nouveau poisson du musée s'appelait un $croqueroche$... C'est parce qu'il mange des cailloux ?
russian: Эррол сказал, что новая рыбка в музее называется $камнегрыз$... потому что она жует камни?
bulgarian: Errol said that new fish over at the Museum is called a $Rockbiter$... on account of it chews up rocks?

english: I don't get it!
french: Je ne comprends pas !
russian: Ничего не понимаю!
bulgarian: I don't get it!

english: Errol told me that the $Shale Grass$ at the Museum isn't made of shale at all! It's grass!
french: Errol m'a dit que l'$herbe de schiste$ du musée n'était pas du tout composée de schiste. C'est juste de l'herbe !
russian: Эррол сказал, что $сланец-трава$ в музее вообще не из сланца! Это трава!
bulgarian: Errol told me that the $Shale Grass$ at the Museum isn't made of shale at all! It's grass!

english: Would've been handy back when I worked the Mines.
french: Ça m'aurait bien servi quand j'étais mineur.
russian: Вот бы он был у меня, когда я работал в шахтах.
bulgarian: Would've been handy back when I worked the Mines.

english: Too bad about the earthquake messing it up, huh?
french: Dommage que tout soit sens dessus dessous à cause du tremblement de terre, pas vrai ?!
russian: Жаль, что землетрясение всё испортило, хм?
bulgarian: Too bad about the earthquake messing it up, huh?

english: Errol showed me that $Shortcut Scroll$ you dropped off at the Museum, [Ari]!
french: Errol m'a montré le $parchemin de raccourci$ que tu as offert au musée, [Ari] !
russian:
Эррол показал мне $свиток короткого пути$, который ты

принесли

принеслапринёспринесло в музей, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Errol showed me that $Shortcut Scroll$ you dropped off at the Museum, [Ari]!

english: That's kinda how I think of you, [Ari]! A good omen! But for all of Mistria!
french: C'est un peu comme ça que je te vois, [Ari] ! Tu es un bon présage. Mais pour tout Mistria !
russian: А я считаю, что это ты, [Ari]! Доброе предзнаменование для всей Мистрии!
bulgarian: That's kinda how I think of you, [Ari]! A good omen! But for all of Mistria!

english: Whoa, are you a squid?
french: Waouh, attends... tu es un calmar ?
russian: Погоди-ка, а ты, случайно, не кальмар?
bulgarian: Whoa, are you a squid?

english: You caught that $Silver Squid$ over at the Museum, right? Terithia says it's a good omen...
french: C'est toi qui as attrapé ce $calmar argenté$ qu'on trouve au musée, non ? Terithia dit que c'est un bon présage...
russian:
Это ты

поймали

поймалапоймалпоймало $серебряного кальмара$, который у нас в музее? Теризия говорит, это доброе предзнаменование...
bulgarian: You caught that $Silver Squid$ over at the Museum, right? Terithia says it's a good omen...

english: I want to know!
french: J'aimerais bien savoir.
russian: Интересно было бы узнать!
bulgarian: I want to know!

english: That $Tiny Volcano$ at the Museum... do you think it makes tiny basalt? Tiny rhyolite?
french: Ce $mini volcan$ au musée... Tu crois qu'il est fait de mini basalte ? Ou de mini rhyolite ?
russian: Я увидел в музее $вулканчик$... Как ты думаешь, из него получается крошечный базальт? Крошечный риолит?
bulgarian: That $Tiny Volcano$ at the Museum... do you think it makes tiny basalt? Tiny rhyolite?

english: If I look at it too long, I start to feel kinda funny.
french: Si je la fixe trop longtemps, je commence à me sentir tout drôle.
russian: Я неуютно себя чувствую, если долго в него всматриваюсь.
bulgarian: If I look at it too long, I start to feel kinda funny.

english: You know, normally I like rocks, but that $Void Stone$ over at the Museum...
french: Tu sais, en général, j'aime toutes les roches, mais cette $pierre du néant$, au musée...
russian: Знаешь, я обычно люблю камни, но этот $пустотный камень$ в музее...
bulgarian: You know, normally I like rocks, but that $Void Stone$ over at the Museum...
